title: Default-Argument Score
prompt_md:
## Goal
Give `Score` one constructor that works whether or not the caller supplies a value. With no argument, the score defaults to 100; with an argument, it uses that value.

## Input
One line: one integer `N` (0 ≤ N ≤ 1000).

## Output
Two lines:
```
Default: 100
Provided: N
```

## Task
Write a single `Score` constructor that takes one `int` parameter with a default argument (lesson 14.11), so that `Score{}` starts at 100 and `Score{ N }` starts at `N`. The `getValue()` accessor and the driver in `main` are provided.

title: Account With an Empty State
prompt_md:
## Goal
Model a bank `Account` that can be created two ways: with no arguments (an empty account) or with an owner name and a starting balance.

## Input
One line: a name (a single word) and an integer balance, separated by a space.

## Output
Two lines:
```
Empty account: none, 0
Custom account: <name>, <balance>
```

## Task
Write two constructors for `Account` (lesson 14.11): a default constructor (no parameters) that sets the owner to `"none"` and the balance to `0`, and a second constructor that takes an owner name and a balance. Remember that once you write the second constructor the compiler stops supplying a default one, so the no-argument constructor must be written by hand. The accessors and the driver in `main` are provided.

test_cases.label: Sample: typical account
test_cases.expected_stdout:
Empty account: none, 0
Custom account: Alice, 500

test_cases.expected_stdout:

Custom account: Bob, 0
